source_text: Καὶ πρῶτόν γε ἕφασκες, ὅτι ἡνίκα διελεγόμην τῷ ἑταίρῳ ἡμῶν Βάσσῳ, καὶ συνεχρώμην τῇ τοῦ Δανιὴλ νεωτέρου προφητεύσαντος περὶ τῶν κατὰ τὴν Σωσάνναν Γραφῇ, τοῦτο πεποίηκα, ὡς λανθάνοντός με τοῦ μέρους τοῦ βιβλίου κεκιβδηλευμένου ὅντος. Καὶ ἕλεγες τὴν περικοπὴν ταύτην ἐπαινεῖν μέν πως ὥς τι χαρίεν· ἔφασκες δὲ ψέγειν ὡς οὖσαν σύγγραμμα νεωτερικὸν καὶ πεπλασμένον· καὶ ὅτι, ὡς οὐδὲ Φιλιστίων ὁ μῖμος, ἐχρήσατο ἀναπλάσας τὸ συγγραμμάτιον τῇ τῶν ὀνομάτων γειτνιάσει, πρίνου πρὸς πρίσιν, καὶ σχίνου πρὸς σχίσιν· Ἅπερ κατὰ μὲν τὴν Ἐλλήνων φωνὴντοιαῦτα εἶναι δοκεῖ, κατὰ δὲ τὴν Ἑβραίων οὐδαμῶς. Ἴσθι τοίνυν πρὸς ταῦτα, τί χρὴ ἡμᾶς πράττειν οὐ περὶ τῶν κατὰ Σωσάνναν μόνον, ἐν μὲν τῷ καθʼ Ἕλληνας Ἑλληνικῷ φερομένων ἐν πάσῃ Ἐκκλησίᾳ Χριστοῦ, παρὰ δὲ Ἑβραίοις μὴ κειμένων· οὐδὲ περὶ τῶν, ὡς ἔφασκες, ἄλλων δύο περικοπῶν τῶν ἐπὶ τέλει τοῦ βιβλίου περί τε τῶν κατὰ τὸν Βὴλ, καὶ τὸν δράκοντα ἀναγεγραμμένων, οὐδ’ αὐτῶν ἐν τῷ Δανιὴλ τῶν Ἑβραίων γεγραμμένων· ἀλλὰ καὶ περὶ ἄλλων μυρίων, ἃ κατὰ τὴν μετριότητα ἡμῶν τοῖς Ἑβραῖκοῖς συγκρίναντες ἀντιγράφοις τὰ ἡμέτερα. πολλαχοῦ εὕρομεν. Ἐν μὲν γὰρ αὐτῷ τῷ Δανιὴλ περὶ τῆς καμίνου τῆς καομένης, τὸ « πεπεδημένοι » εὕρομεν· ἐν δὲ τοῖς ἡμετέροις ἀντιγράφοις περισσεύοντα παρὰ τὰ ἐν τοῖς Ἑβραϊκοῖς ἕπη οὐκ ὀλίγα, ὥν ἀρχὴ κατὰ μέν τινα τῶν φερομένων ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις ἦν οὕτως· « Προσηύξαντο Ἀνανίας, καὶ Ἀζαρίας, καὶ Μισαὴλ, καὶ ὕμνησαν τὸν Κύριον· » ἕως τοῦ « Εὐλογεῖτε πάντες οἱ σεβόμενοι Κύριον τὸν Θεὸν τῶν θεῶν. Ὑμνεῖτε καὶ ἐξομολογεῖσθε, ὅτι εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τὸ ἕλεος αὐτοῦ, καὶ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τῶν αἰώνων. Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἀκοῦσαι τὸν βασιλέα ὑμνούντων αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐθεώρει αὐτοὺς ζῶντας. » Κατὰ δὲ ἕτερα· « Καὶ περιεπάτουν ἐν μέσῳ τῆς φλογὸς ὑμνοῦντες τὸν Θεὸν, καὶ εὐλογοῦντες τὸν Κύριον· » ἕως τοῦ· « Εὐλογεῖτε πάντες οἱ σεβόμενοι τὸν Κύριον τὸν Θεὸν τῶν θεῶν. Ὑμνεῖτε καὶ ἐξομολογεῖσθε, ὅτι εἰς πάντας τοὺς αἰῶνας τὸ ελεος αὐτοῦ.» Συνῆπτο δὲ ἐν τοῖς Ἑβραῖκοῖς τό· « Καὶ οἱ ἄνδρες ἐκεῖνοι οἱ τρεῖς Σεδρὰχ, Μισὰχ, Ἀβδενεγὼ, ἔπεσον εἰς μέσον τοῦ πυρὸς πεπεδημένοι· » τό τε « Ὁ βασιλεὺς ὁ Nαβουχοδονόσορ ἐθαύμασε, καὶ ἀνέστη ἐν σπουδῇ, καὶ ἀπεκρίθη, καὶ εἶπε τοῖς μεγιστᾶσιν αὐτοῦ.» Οὕτω γὰρ Ἀκύλας δουλεύων τῇ Ἑβραῖκῇ λέξει ἐκδέδωκεν εἰπών· φιλοτιμότερον πεπιστευμένος παρὰ Ἰουδαίοις ἡρμηνευκέναι τὴν Γραφήν· ᾧ μάλιστα εἰώθασι οἱ ἀγνοοῦντες τὴν Ἑβραίων διάλεκτον χρῆσθαι, ὡς πάντων μᾶλλον ἐπιτετευγμένῳ. Τὰ δὲ παρʼ ἡμῖν ἀντίγραφα, ὧν καὶ τὰς λέξεις ἐξεθέμην, τὸ μὲν ἦν κατὰ τοὺς Ο΄· τὸ δὲ ἕτερον καοτί καὶ ὥσπερ παρʼ ἀμφοτέροις ἕκειτο τὸ περὶ τὴν Σωσάνναν, ὡς σὺ φὴς, πλάσμα, καὶ αἱ τελευταῖαι ἐν τῷ Δανιὴλ περικοπαί· οὕτω καὶ ταῦτα ἐν ἕπεσιν,ὡς τοχασμῷ εἰπεῖν, τυγχάνοντα διακοσίοις καὶ πρός.
pass_a_gloss: And first you were saying that when I was discussing with our companion Bassus, and I was using the scripture of Daniel the younger prophet who prophesied about the things concerning Susanna, I did this as one who was ignorant of the part of the book that had been falsified. And you were praising this passage in some way as something charming, but you were condemning it as being a modern and fabricated writing. And that, just like Philistion the mime, he used it by rearranging the writing with the proximity of the names, 'prinos' to 'prinos' and 'schinos' to 'schisis'. Which seems to be the case in the Greek language, but not at all in the Hebrew language. Know then what we should do, not only concerning the things about Susanna, which are being carried in the whole Church of Christ in the Greek language, but not found among the Hebrews. Nor about the other two passages, as you said, at the end of the book, concerning the things written about Bel and the dragon, which are not even written in the Hebrew Daniel. But also about many other things, which, comparing our copies with the Hebrew ones, we have found in many places. For in the same Daniel, concerning the burning furnace, we found 'having been bound'. And in our copies, there are many verses that are excessive, beyond what is in the Hebrew, the beginning of which, according to some of the ones being carried in the churches, was as follows: 'Ananias and Azarias and Misael prayed and hymned the Lord', until 'Bless, all you who fear the Lord, the God of gods. Hymn and confess, for his mercy is forever and ever.' And it happened when the king heard them hymning and saw them alive. According to others, 'And they were walking in the midst of the fire, hymning God and blessing the Lord', until 'Bless, all you who fear the Lord, the God of gods. Hymn and confess, for his mercy is forever.' But in the Hebrew, it was added that 'those three men, Sedrach, Misach, and Abdenego, fell into the midst of the fire, having been bound'. And 'the king Nabuchodonosor was amazed and rose up in haste and answered and said to his nobles'. For Akylas, serving the Hebrew language, has published it, saying that he has translated the scripture more faithfully than the Jews. Whom the ignorant of the Hebrew dialect are accustomed to use, as if he has attained the greatest accuracy. But our copies, which I have exhibited, one was according to the Seventy, and the other was also, as it seems, from both, concerning the passage about Susanna, as you say, a fabrication, and the last passages in Daniel. So also these things, in verses, as it were by chance, are found in about two hundred places.
pass_b_english: First you said that when I was discussing with our companion Bassus and cited the scripture of the younger prophet Daniel about the things concerning Susanna, I did so as if unaware that part of the book had been falsified. You called this passage charming in a way and praised it, but you also condemned it as a modern and fabricated writing. You claimed that, just like Philistion the mime, he rearranged the little book by the proximity of the names — 'prinos' to 'prinos' and 'schinos' to 'schisis' — which works in Greek but not at all in Hebrew. So understand what we must do, not only about the things concerning Susanna, which are read in every Church of Christ in the Greek language but are not found among the Hebrews, nor about the other two passages, as you said, at the end of the book, concerning Bel and the dragon, which are not even written in the Hebrew Daniel, but also about many other things. Comparing our copies with the Hebrew ones, we have found many such places. For in Daniel itself, concerning the burning furnace, we found the phrase 'having been bound'. And in our copies there are verses that exceed what is in the Hebrew, not a few. The beginning of some of these, as carried in the churches, ran: 'Ananias and Azarias and Misael prayed and hymned the Lord,' until 'Bless, all you who fear the Lord, the God of gods. Hymn and confess, for his mercy is forever and ever.' And it happened when the king heard them hymning and saw them alive. According to others: 'And they were walking in the midst of the fire, hymning God and blessing the Lord,' until 'Bless, all you who fear the Lord, the God of gods. Hymn and confess, for his mercy is forever.' But in the Hebrew it was added that 'those three men, Sedrach, Misach, and Abdenego, fell into the midst of the fire, having been bound,' and 'the king Nebuchadnezzar was amazed and rose up in haste and answered and said to his nobles.' For Aquila, serving the Hebrew text, has published it, saying that he translated the Scripture more faithfully than the Jews — whom those who do not know the Hebrew dialect are accustomed to use, as if he had achieved the greatest accuracy. But our copies, whose readings I have exhibited, one was according to the Seventy, and the other also, as it seems, from both, contained the passage about Susanna, which you call a fabrication, and the last passages in Daniel. So these things too, in verses, as it were by chance, are found in about two hundred places.
notes: No specific verses from Daniel are quoted or alluded to in the Greek text.
